claude.untrusted_cwd: claude --bg in an untrusted directory exits 1 in 0.61 s with 'Workspace not trusted...'; it does not stall on a modal
claude.session_id_prebinding: NOT available under --bg: 'warning: --bg manages the session id; ignoring --session-id'. The daemon assigns the id and prints the short form on stdout ('backgrounded · cb28f684 · <name>'); agents --json gives the full sessionId
claude.turn_1: argv prompt delivered and answered (HOST-PROBE-OK, claude-opus-5-5); transcript at ~/.claude/projects/<proj>/<sessionId>.jsonl; agents --json then reports state=done status=idle
claude.resume_while_loaded: claude --bg --resume <id> '<msg>' on a loaded idle session does NOT deliver: it starts a COPY with a new sessionId (168d03db-3ffc-43f4-b588-1895844cd4fa) under the SAME --name, exit 0, the note only on stdout. The copy carries the full history and answered the message. This is a silent fork.
claude.stop_then_resume: claude stop <id> then claude --bg --resume <id> '<msg>' delivers into the SAME sessionId and transcript ('woke session cb28f684 with its saved options (--name, --model)'); answered HOST-PROBE-TURN-2. Idle -> working -> done/idle in ~8 s
claude.rm: claude rm <id> removes the session from agents --json --all but leaves the transcript on disk
claude.status_fields: background rows: id, sessionId, cwd, kind=background, startedAt, name, state (working|done), status (busy|idle|absent); pid present only while loaded. No parent field.

codex.quota: available again 2026-10-25 (exec turn completed); supersedes the 2026-10-30 retry date recorded earlier
codex.exec_turn_1: codex exec --json -s read-only '<prompt>' completed in 8.09 s; first event is thread.started with thread_id 01a173d2-f5aa-7193-9ef8-115c37743052, so the id is known at launch without database discovery
codex.queue_without_live_session: codex queue --thread <id> on a thread no process holds: exit 0, 'Queued message ...', but NO turn started (turn count stayed 1 over ~30 s). At the next exec resume the queued text was injected as a user item (rollout line 22) immediately before the new prompt (line 26), and the model answered only the new prompt. So queue is a deposit that merges into the next turn, not a wake, unless a live session holds the thread (the earlier tmux probe observed a wake into an idle TUI session).
codex.exec_resume: codex exec --json resume <id> '<msg>' runs a new turn on the SAME thread id (thread_turns count 1 -> 2, both completed)
codex.daemon_hosted_thread: not_established. The shared app-server daemon is running (codex app-server daemon version: status running, socket ~/.codex/app-server-control/app-server-control.sock) and its protocol has thread/start, turn/start, thread/loaded/list. A newline-delimited JSON-RPC initialize sent through 'codex app-server proxy' got no reply within 10 s; the control socket takes ws-style addresses (--remote unix://), so proxy likely relays websocket frames. Not pursued; no thread was started (no rollout contains the probe prompt).
codex.status_fields: no machine-readable session listing from the CLI (codex agents is a TUI). Turn status is readable from ~/.codex/thread_history_1.sqlite thread_turns (status inProgress|completed|failed).

design_consequences.identity_ordering: both hosts now share launch -> learn id -> post handoff -> deliver. The Claude advantage recorded under tmux (pre-minted id) does not exist under --bg.
design_consequences.delivery: Claude: stop-then-resume of an IDLE session; never resume a loaded one (silent fork). Codex: exec resume per turn; queue only as a deposit. A role blocked in a board wait is busy, so self-wake by board wait remains the primary path for a live root.
design_consequences.fork_hazard: the Claude copy-on-resume is a host-level instance of the fork case the generation guard targets: a wake that names a loaded session creates a second live instance under one role name with exit 0. The adapter must check status=idle and loaded state before resume, and must detect 'started a copy' in the output and treat it as a defect.
design_consequences.liveness: Claude: agents --json state/status by sessionId. Codex: thread_turns status by thread_id; a process-level liveness for exec turns is the exec process itself.
